question: What are the current, minimum and maximum timer resolutions, and which processes hold a request?
reason: the current timer resolution has no documented read a 5.1 script can make: timeGetDevCaps (https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/timeapi/nf-timeapi-timegetdevcaps) returns the minimum and maximum period only and is a native call; the inbox report that lists the platform timer resolution and the outstanding requests is "powercfg /energy", which observes the system for 60 seconds and writes a report file, and Microsoft documents it for an idle system (https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-hardware/design/device-experiences/powercfg-command-line-options); it is left to the elevated task (collectors/windows/README.md, Needs elevation). "powercfg /requests" lists power requests, not timer requests, and is not timer evidence. Nothing here requests a timer period

documented_paths.why_not_used: native call; minimum and maximum only
observes the system for 60 seconds and writes a report; Microsoft documents it for an idle system; left to the elevated task
lists power requests (display, system, away mode), which are not timer resolution requests

follow_up: the elevated task runs powercfg /energy into the bundle, or a later collector gets a documented native read; the timer helper process and its command line are recorded by timer_helper_process meanwhile
